paragraphs: A function in C is a named block of statements that performs a specific task. Its definition has this syntax:

items.label: return_type
items.text: The type of value returned; use void for no returned value.

items.label: function_name
items.text: A valid identifier used to call the function.

items.label: parameter_list
items.text: Inputs declared with their types; use void for no parameters.

items.label: Body
items.text: Statements inside { } perform the task.

items.label: return
items.text: Sends a value to the caller. A void function may use return; or reach its closing brace.

blocks.text: Here sum accepts two integer parameters, adds them and returns an integer result.

paragraphs: A prime number is an integer greater than 1 with exactly two positive divisors. It is enough to test divisors up to the square root of n.

blocks.text: Algorithm

items.text: Read the integer n.
If n < 2, report “Not prime” and stop.
Set d = 2.
While d ≤ n / d: if n % d == 0, report “Not prime” and stop; otherwise increase d by 1.
If no divisor was found, report “Prime” and stop.

blocks.text: Flowchart logic (text layout)

rows: Yes → output Not prime → Stop. No → set d = 2 (process rectangle).
No → output Prime → Stop. Yes → test divisibility.
Yes → output Not prime → Stop. No → d = d + 1 (process rectangle), then return to the divisor-limit decision.

blocks.text: For n = 13, divisors 2 and 3 leave remainders 1 and 1; the next divisor 4 exceeds 13/4, so 13 is prime. For n = 12, divisor 2 leaves remainder 0, so 12 is not prime. Testing d ≤ n/d avoids forming d*d.

endsem-2026-1-a.authority: PankusDesk-authored exam answer based on the supplied notes; C11 examples
endsem-2026-1-a.basis_label: Priyanka class notes, supplemented by senior notes

source_trace.priority: Priyanka → senior KB → general PPS knowledge
source_trace.authored_application: Prime algorithm from senior notes; flowchart symbol meanings from Priyanka. Text layout follows the existing worksheet convention under the drawing freeze.

endsem-2026-1-a.final_answer: Result: 13 is prime; 12 and every integer below 2 are not prime.

paragraphs: Type conversion changes a value from one data type to another. C performs some conversions automatically; the programmer requests others using a cast.

blocks.text: The compiler applies conversion rules during assignment or expression evaluation without an explicit cast. For example, assigning int 5 to float produces 5.0.
Syntax: (type) expression. Casting sum before division makes the calculation floating-point, so 5/2 becomes 2.5 rather than the integer result 2.

rows: Can lose precision or fractional information.
Can also lose information; the cast does not guarantee safety.

blocks.text: For a representable floating value, conversion to int discards the fractional part toward zero: (int)3.9 is 3. A cast changes the expression’s type, not the declared type of the original variable.

endsem-2026-1-b.authority: PankusDesk-authored exam answer based on the supplied notes; C11 examples

paragraphs: Branching selects or transfers control to a part of a program. A condition is false when zero and true when nonzero. The main selection forms are if and switch; goto is an unconditional jump.

blocks.text: Executes its body only when the condition is true. The example prints Positive; if n were not positive, the body would be skipped.
Selects exactly one of two branches. The remainder test classifies 7 as odd.
Places a decision inside another branch. The example compares three values and prints the greatest, 12. Braces make the intended else associations clear.
Tests conditions in order, executes the first matching branch, and skips the remaining alternatives. The final else handles an unmatched case; this example prints Zero.
The controlling expression has integer type, and case labels are distinct integer constants. break prevents fall-through, and default handles unmatched values. The example prints Add.
Transfers control to a labelled statement in the same function. It is an unconditional branch, not a substitute for every conditional statement. This example prints Invalid.

endsem-2026-2.authority: PankusDesk-authored exam answer based on the supplied notes; C11 examples

paragraphs: An array is a collection of elements of the same type stored contiguously. Elements are selected by zero-based indices. Arrays may have one or more dimensions.

blocks.text: General declaration: data_type array_name[size];. A one-dimensional array is a linear sequence; int a[5]; has valid indices 0 through 4.

blocks.code:
int a[5] = {10, 20, 30, 40, 50}; /* full initialization */
int b[5] = {10, 20};             /* remaining elements are 0 */
int c[] = {10, 20, 30};          /* size inferred as 3 */

blocks.text: Access a single element as a[i]. a[0] is 10 and a[4] is 50. An automatic array without an initializer must have its elements assigned before they are read.
General declaration: data_type array_name[rows][columns];. A two-dimensional array is an array of row arrays. int m[3][3]; contains nine integers; m[i][j] selects row i, column j.

The first dimension may be inferred from an initializer, but the column extent is retained. C stores rows in row-major order: all of row 0, then row 1, and so on. Valid indices satisfy 0 ≤ i < rows and 0 ≤ j < columns.
Accessing the initialized matrix
Nested loops visit every row and column; print a[i][j], which is an element, rather than a[i], which is a row.

endsem-2026-3.authority: PankusDesk-authored exam answer based on the supplied notes; C11 examples

paragraphs: Loops repeat a block of statements while a controlling condition permits it. C has while, do–while and for loops.

blocks.text: The condition is checked before each iteration, so the body may execute zero times. Initialize the control variable before the loop and update it appropriately inside. This example prints 1 through 5.

The body is entered before the first condition check, so it is entered at least once. The trailing semicolon is required. This example sums the first 20 positive even numbers, 2 through 40, obtaining 420.
Initialization executes once. Then the condition is tested, the body runs, the update executes, and the condition is tested again. This example multiplies 1 through 5, obtaining 120.
break exits the nearest loop. continue skips to the next iteration’s control step; in a for loop it proceeds to the update expression.

paragraphs: Pass the addresses of the two integers to a function with int* parameters. Use the indirection operator to modify the original values.

items.text: Call swap(&a, &b), so x points to a and y points to b.
Save *x in temp before overwriting it.
Assign *x = *y and then *y = temp. The changes remain in the caller after return.

blocks.text: Trace for a = 10 and b = 20: temp becomes 10; *x becomes 20; *y becomes 10. C passes the pointer values by value; writing through them changes the caller’s integers.

paragraphs: Functions are classified by whether they accept arguments and whether they return a value. void indicates no returned value; (void) declares no parameters.

blocks.text: The caller supplies both operands; the function prints the result. Call: add_print(3, 4);.
The function reads operands and prints the result internally. Call: read_print();.
The caller supplies operands and receives the result. Call: int result = add_return(3, 4);.
The function reads operands internally and returns their sum. Call: int result = read_return();.
These function definitions use <stdio.h> and <stdlib.h>. For the examples, assume small integer operands whose sum fits int. Supplying 3 and 4 gives 7 in each category.

paragraphs: Selection sort repeatedly finds the minimum element in the unsorted part of an array and exchanges it with the first element of that part.

blocks.text: Algorithm

items.text: Read N and the N array elements.
For each position i from 0 to N − 2, set min_index = i.
Scan positions j = i + 1 through N − 1. If a[j] < a[min_index], update min_index = j.
Exchange a[i] and a[min_index] if they are different positions. The prefix through i is now sorted.
After all passes, display the array.

blocks.text: The smallest remaining element is selected on every pass, so the sorted prefix grows by one. The algorithm makes N(N−1)/2 comparisons: Θ(N²) time in best and worst cases and O(1) extra space. The ordinary swap-based version is not stable.

endsem-2026-6.authority: PankusDesk-authored exam answer based on the supplied notes; C11 examples

paragraphs: A pointer is an object that stores an address. Its type specifies the kind of object it can point to, such as int* for an integer object.

blocks.text: Declaration
Initialization

blocks.code:
int value = 25;
int *p = &value;

items.label: int *p
items.text: Declares p as a pointer to int.

items.label: &value
items.text: Obtains the address of the existing integer object.

items.label: *p
items.text: Accesses that integer through the pointer; reading *p gives 25.

items.label: Assignment through the pointer
items.text: *p = 40; changes value to 40.

blocks.text: A declaration alone does not give a local pointer a valid target. Initialize it before dereferencing it, and use it only while the pointed-to object exists. In int *p, q;, p is a pointer but q is an int.

endsem-2026-7-a.authority: PankusDesk-authored exam answer based on the supplied notes; C11 examples

paragraphs: The unary * operator is the indirection (dereference) operator. Applied to a valid pointer, it accesses the object at the pointed-to address.

items.text: value is initialized to 25.
&value supplies its address to p.
*p reads the integer stored at that address, so both output lines show 25.

blocks.text: The * in int *p declares a pointer; the * in printf’s *p expression dereferences that pointer. No numeric memory address needs to be assumed.

paragraphs: A structure can be passed as a complete value or by passing its address. The function’s parameter type determines how it accesses the record.

blocks.text: A parameter such as struct Time t receives a copy of the caller’s structure. Access members using t.hours, t.minutes and t.seconds. Changes to that copy do not alter the caller’s structure.

A parameter such as const struct Time *t receives a pointer to the original record. Call with &time_object and access members using ->. A non-const pointer can modify the original members; const is appropriate here because the conversion only reads them. The pointer itself is still passed by value.

rows: No; the pointer value is copied.

blocks.text: There are 3600 seconds in an hour and 60 in a minute, so total = 3600 × hours + 60 × minutes + seconds.
For 1 hour, 2 minutes, 3 seconds: 3600 × 1 + 60 × 2 + 3 = 3723. Both functions calculate the same result without changing the input record.

endsem-2026-8.authority: PankusDesk-authored exam answer based on the supplied notes; C11 examples

paragraphs: Preprocessor directives are handled before compilation of the resulting C source. #include brings in header content, while #define creates a macro.

blocks.text: Syntax: #include <header> or #include "header". Standard headers provide declarations, types and macros needed by the program.

blocks.code:
#include <stdio.h>   /* declares printf, scanf, etc. */
#include "myheader.h" /* a program-supplied header */

blocks.text: Angle brackets select the implementation’s header search mechanism. Quotes are normally used for a program’s own header, searched using the implementation’s quoted-header rules. Including a header is preprocessing, not linking a library implementation.
Syntax: #define name replacement_text. The preprocessor replaces uses of the macro name with its replacement tokens.
Here PI is a symbolic constant, so the expression becomes 3.14 × 2.0 × 2.0 = 12.56. Do not put a semicolon at the end of this definition; replacement happens before the C expression is compiled.

paragraphs: Read the filename, open the file in text-read mode, then copy each successfully read character to the screen.

items.text: Use fgets to read a filename, including spaces, and remove the input newline.
Open with fopen(name, "r") and check for NULL.
Read with fgetc until EOF, storing its result in int so EOF remains distinguishable.
Write each character with putchar, check for read errors, and close the stream.

paragraphs: C provides stream-status functions for errors, positioning functions for random access, and argc/argv parameters for command-line input.

blocks.text: Always check fopen against NULL before using a stream. Check read/write results and fclose for failure.

rows: Tests whether an I/O error indicator is set.
Tests whether the end-of-file indicator is set after a read reaches the end.
Reports the current errno error with a message.

blocks.text: Use the read result as the loop condition; while (!feof(fp)) can process stale data because EOF is detected by a read.
Sequential access processes data in order. Random access changes the file position explicitly.

rows: fseek(fp, offset, origin): returns 0 on success; origins are SEEK_SET, SEEK_CUR and SEEK_END.
long position = ftell(fp): returns a position indicator, or -1L on failure.
rewind(fp): moves to the beginning and clears error/EOF indicators; returns no value.

blocks.text: For portable text-stream seeking, use offset 0 or a position previously returned by ftell with SEEK_SET. Arbitrary byte offsets belong to suitable binary streams.

Use int main(int argc, char *argv[]). argc is the argument count; argv holds argument strings and argv[argc] is NULL. When argc > 0, argv[0] represents the program name if available; argv[1] is the first supplied argument.
For ./program hello, argc is 2 and argv[1] is "hello", so the output is hello. Check the count before accessing an argument.
